367783.title: Realizability of circular extensions for connected DC graphs
367783.ordinary_result_or_gap: Source Conjecture 1.8; cyclic extensions give combinatorial fibers, not parameter feasibility. Need simultaneous positive cursor speeds and jump-time inequalities realizing every order. No finite obstruction or full parameter construction obtained.
367783.literal_statement: Fix $N$ and let $G\in\operatorname{DC}_N$ be a connected DC graph. Let $Z'_G$ be the partial cyclic order obtained by requiring that, for every maximal edge $(i,j)$ of $G$, the tuples $(i,i+1,\ldots,j)$, $(i,i-1,j)$ and $(j,i,j+1)$ are $Z'_G$-chains. A circular extension of $Z'_G$ is a total cyclic order extending this partial cyclic order. **Realizability conjecture.** For every connected DC graph $G\in\operatorname{DC}_N$, every circular extension of $Z'_G$ arises as the total cyclic order of cursor jumps for some value of parameters $(\underline a,\underline p)\in P_G$. The map from total cyclic orders to connected DC graphs is known to have fibers described by the circular extensions of $Z'_G$; the conjecture asks whether every order in such a fiber is realized by model parameters.

367940.title: Second-order Eulerian formula conjecture for flattened Fubini rankings
367940.ordinary_result_or_gap: At j=2 the literal left side s(5,1)=1: one strict ascent run forces all ranks distinct, hence the unique ranking 12345. E2(5,0)=1, and 1122335544 is a Stirling permutation with exactly one descent, so E2(5,1)>=1. The RHS is >=3. Source Table 2 already prints s(5,1)=1. The source itself says maximal runs whereas j-1 is not maximal. This resolves only a printed inconsistent formula, not the intended enumeration; zero credit.
367940.literal_statement:
Let $\mathrm{FR}_n$ denote the set of Fubini rankings on $n$ competitors, and let $\mathrm{flat\_runs}_k(\mathrm{FR}_n)$ denote the flattened Fubini rankings with $k$ runs of ascents. Define

$$
s(n,k)=|\mathrm{flat\_runs}_k(\mathrm{FR}_n)|.
$$

Let $E_2(a,b)$ denote the second-order Eulerian numbers. **Second-order Eulerian formula conjecture.** For every relevant integer $j$,

$$
s(2j+1,j-1)=\sum_{i=0}^{j-1}E_2(2j+1,i)2^i.
$$

The source identifies the second-order Eulerian numbers with OEIS A340556 and states that proving this formula, as well as finding formulas for $s(n,k)$ in general, remains open.

368222.title: The colourful induced-subgraph conjecture for forests
368222.ordinary_result_or_gap: Full forest quantifier and epsilon-dependent positive delta. Iteratively deleting low-colour portions need not preserve a linear fraction uniformly; clique-number-dependent source bounds do not give delta depending only on the forest and epsilon. No viable full route.
368222.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. For a vertex $v\in V(G)$, write $N_G[v]=N_G(v)\cup\{v\}$, and call $G$ **$\varepsilon$-colourful** if

$$
\chi(G\setminus N_G[v])<\varepsilon\chi(G)
$$

for every $v\in V(G)$. For an induced subgraph $F$ of $G$, use the same definition with $F$ in place of $G$. **Colourful induced-subgraph conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$ and every forest $T$, there exists $\delta>0$ such that every $T$-free graph $G$ has an $\varepsilon$-colourful induced subgraph $F$ with $\chi(F)\ge\delta\chi(G)$. This asserts the existence of a locally dense induced subgraph carrying a linear proportion of the chromatic number. It is known for $T=P_4$ and for stars, but the source says it is undecided for $T=P_5$ and even for the two-edge matching.

368223.title: The locally dense induced-subgraph conjecture for $P_5$-free graphs
368223.ordinary_result_or_gap: For every P5-free graph a single positive universal delta is required. Passing to a chromatic-critical graph controls degrees, not neighbourhood chromatic numbers. Source polynomial-versus-linear pairs still depend on clique number. No full constant established.
368223.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. For an induced subgraph $F$ of $G$ and $v\in V(F)$, let $N_F(v)$ be the neighbours of $v$ in $F$. **$P_5$ local-density conjecture.** There exists $\delta>0$ such that every $P_5$-free graph $G$ has an induced subgraph $F$ satisfying

$$
\chi(F)\ge\delta\chi(G)
$$

and

$$
\chi(N_F(v))\ge\delta\chi(F)
$$

for every $v\in V(F)$. This is presented as a weaker, particularly interesting special case of the colourful induced-subgraph conjecture; the source does not report a resolution.

368225.title: Acyclic system conjecture for mixed subdivisions
368225.ordinary_result_or_gap: Latest primary source explicitly calls the general acyclic-system conjecture false. Read matching-ensemble definition/translation and the statement distinguishing it from the still-open spread-out conjecture. No new claim: exact printed counterexample and original refutation proof not fully audited here, so public refutation is source-reported rather than independently replayed.
368225.literal_statement: Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $[d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}$. A **system of permutations** records the permutations obtained from the boundary data of a mixed subdivision of $n\Delta_{d-1}$, and it is **acyclic** when it contains no forbidden cyclic pattern. **Acyclic system conjecture.** A system of permutations comes from a mixed subdivision of $n\Delta_{d-1}$ if and only if it is acyclic. This extends the stated two-dimensional acyclic-system theorem to arbitrary $d$; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

368229.title: Rigidity conjecture for special mixed graphs without satellites
368229.ordinary_result_or_gap: No-satellites must force graph reconstruction from an arbitrary abstract T-RAAG isomorphism. Known Droms and universal-sinkhole cases do not reconstruct arbitrary special mixed graphs. No concrete full route; source-definition/proof coverage incomplete.
368229.literal_statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a special mixed graph. A **satellite** of a sinkhole $a$ is a vertex at distance $2$ from $a$ such that every vertex joined to it is also joined to $a$. The associated T-RAAG $T(\Gamma)$ is called **rigid** when its isomorphism type determines the associated mixed graph.

**Rigidity conjecture.** If $\Gamma$ has no satellites, then it is rigid.

The paper proves that rigidity implies the absence of satellites for special mixed graphs, and proves the converse for Droms mixed graphs and for special mixed graphs having a sinkhole joined to every other vertex. The conjecture asks whether the converse holds for all special mixed graphs.

368458.title: The pivot containment conjecture
368458.ordinary_result_or_gap: Conjecture 11.13 concerns every singular-space pivot, not merely the pivots constructed from irreducible configurations. Theorem 5.6 supplies only the latter subset. See ORDINARY-ATTEMPTS.md for triangular elimination and steady-recursion gaps.
368458.literal_statement:
Let $W_{2n}$ be the set of words of length $2n$. For a word $w$, let $H(w)$ be its singular-vector space, let $\mathrm{Pvt}(w)$ be the set of pivot sign sequences of a basis of $H(w)$, let $\mathrm{SConf}(w)$ be the set of steady arc configurations, and define $\mu_w$ by

$$
(\mu_w(C))_i=+
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad i\in\operatorname{LC}(C).
$$

**The pivot containment conjecture.** For every $w\in W_{2n}$,

$$
\mathrm{Pvt}(w)\subset\mu_w(\mathrm{SConf}(w)).
$$

The paper explains that irreducible configurations already give the opposite containment into the pivot set, so this conjecture would imply the stated combinatorial consequence. No resolution is given.

368459.title: The irreducible-to-steady arc-configuration conjecture
368459.ordinary_result_or_gap: Conjecture 11.14 asks for a steady configuration with the identical left-end set. Cardinality inequalities and uniqueness on each separate class do not supply the inclusion. See sustained left-end recursion attempt.
368459.literal_statement:
Let $W_{2n}$ be the set of words of length $2n$, let $\mathrm{IConf}(w)$ and $\mathrm{SConf}(w)$ be the irreducible and steady arc configurations of $w$, and let $\mu_w$ record the set of left ends of an arc configuration. **The irreducible-to-steady arc-configuration conjecture.** For every $w\in W_{2n}$,

$$
\mu_w(\mathrm{IConf}(w))\subset\mu_w(\mathrm{SConf}(w)).
$$

Equivalently, every set of left ends arising from an irreducible arc configuration also arises from a steady arc configuration. This is presented as a purely combinatorial consequence of the pivot conjecture; no resolution is stated.

368682.title: The symmetric exchange generation conjecture for unicyclic graph toric ideals
368682.ordinary_result_or_gap: Source Conjecture 5.24 is arbitrary positive capacity vector and every unicyclic graph. Need connectivity of every toric fiber under symmetric exchanges; quadratic generation in source special cases does not settle it. No uniform descent invariant found.
368682.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a unicyclic graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\mathfrak{c} \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}^n$. Write $\operatorname{Ker}(\pi_G^{\mathfrak{c}})$ for the associated toric ideal, and call its binomial generators **symmetric exchange binomials** when they arise from symmetric exchanges. **Symmetric exchange generation conjecture.** For every such $\mathfrak{c}$, the toric ideal

$$
\operatorname{Ker}(\pi_G^{\mathfrak{c}})
$$

is generated by all symmetric exchange binomials of $\operatorname{Ker}(\pi_G^{\mathfrak{c}})$. This conjecture proposes a uniform generation result for toric ideals associated with unicyclic graphs; the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or disproved.

368833.title: The conjecture that continued-fraction sets with matched bounds cover modulo 1
368833.ordinary_result_or_gap: All k and exact modulo-one coverage of real numbers are required. Diameter alone cannot settle this matched-upper/lower sum; interval overlap at finite continued-fraction depth is insufficient without nested admissible limits. No viable full analytic route; parked.
368833.literal_statement:
For $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $F_{\leq k}$ and $F_{\geq k}$ denote the continued-fraction sets whose partial quotients are respectively bounded above by $k$ and bounded below by $k$. Write $A+B=\{a+b:a\in A,b\in B\}$ and $A\equiv\mathbb{R}\mod 1$ when $A+\mathbb{Z}=\mathbb{R}$. **The continued-fraction upper-and-lower conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
F_{\leq 2k}+F_{\geq k}\equiv\mathbb{R}\mod 1.
$$

The directly matched sum $F_{\leq k}+F_{\geq k}$ has diameter less than $1$, so it cannot satisfy the corresponding covering statement. This alternative conjecture is presented as an analogue of the Lüroth-set results and relates to decompositions involving badly and well approximable numbers.

369509.title: The 2-sunflowerability collapse conjecture
369509.ordinary_result_or_gap: Source Definition 2.3 is for infinite structures, quantified over all isomorphic presentations by n-element sets. Ordinary finite sunflower lemmas do not give a self-isomorphic induced substructure. Proposition 2.7 gives indivisibility only. No full n=2-to-all-n bridge.
369509.literal_statement:
A structure ${\mathcal{M}}$ is **2-sunflowerable** if it has the 2-sunflower property, and it is **sunflowerable** if it has the $n$-sunflower property for every relevant finite $n$.

**The 2-sunflowerability collapse conjecture.** If ${\mathcal{M}}$ is a 2-sunflowerable structure, then ${\mathcal{M}}$ is sunflowerable.

The paper notes that $n$-sunflowerability forms a hierarchy and that this hierarchy collapses in all of its examples; whether 2-sunflowerability always implies sunflowerability remains open.

369833.title: Real-part conjecture for tree amplitude functions
369833.ordinary_result_or_gap: Full tree and all configurations in R3 required. Actual amplitude definition uses tensors and symmetrizations; informal leaf peeling is not established as a real-part-preserving positive map. Journal DOI 10.1016/j.geomphys.2026.105993 advertised; published body/corrections unread. No significant proof investment or endpoint.
369833.literal_statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, meaning a connected circuit-free non-oriented finite simple graph, and let $C_T(\mathbb{R}^3)$ be its configuration space. Let $\mathcal{A}_T$ be the associated amplitude function. **Tree real-part conjecture.** For every $\mathbf{x}\in C_T(\mathbb{R}^3)$,

$$
\operatorname{Re}(\mathcal{A}_T(\mathbf{x}))\geq 1.
$$

If true, this conjecture implies the graph-amplitude lower-bound conjecture, and hence also the nonvanishing conjecture, for trees; its resolution is not stated in the supplied text.

370190.title: The Chang–Hsu–Rogers rainbow embedding conjecture
370190.ordinary_result_or_gap: All n-vertex trees and injective labels in Zn with distinct edge sums required. Bounded-degree theorem does not supply unbounded-degree extension; greedy leaf addition can exhaust unused sums. Historical harmonious sibling is not a solution of this stronger endpoint.
370190.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group, and let $K_G$ be the complete graph on vertex set $G$, with each edge $xy$ coloured by $x+y$. A copy is **rainbow** when all its edge colours are distinct.

**Chang–Hsu–Rogers conjecture.** For every $n$-vertex tree $T$, the edge-coloured graph $K_{\mathbb{Z}_n}$ contains a rainbow copy of $T$.

This stronger rainbow-embedding formulation would imply the harmonious labelling conjecture. The paper confirms it for bounded-degree trees, while the general case remains open.

full_parsed_record.title: The Chang–Hsu–Rogers rainbow embedding conjecture
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group, and let $K_G$ be the complete graph on vertex set $G$, with each edge $xy$ coloured by $x+y$. A copy is **rainbow** when all its edge colours are distinct.

**Chang–Hsu–Rogers conjecture.** For every $n$-vertex tree $T$, the edge-coloured graph $K_{\mathbb{Z}_n}$ contains a rainbow copy of $T$.

This stronger rainbow-embedding formulation would imply the harmonious labelling conjecture. The paper confirms it for bounded-degree trees, while the general case remains open.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Alp Müyesser and Alexey Pokrovskiy, “On the Graham–Sloane harmonious labelling conjecture”, arXiv:2509.05280 (2025).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.05280

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2025).

370334.title: $k$-regular bipartite domination number bound
370334.ordinary_result_or_gap: Complete hand refutation with bipartite double of KG(8,2), n=28, k=15, no dominating set of size <=4. All source versions retrieved and v3 exact Conjecture 1 compared with absence in v1,v2,v4,v5. No explicit reason for removal found. Existing bipartite-Kneser domination literature, published correspondence and registry scope remain incomplete: no novelty/significance clearance, no execution. See ORDINARY-PROOF-HOLD.md.
370334.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-regular bipartite graph with bipartition $V(G)=A\cup B$ and $|A|=|B|=n$. Let $\gamma(G)$ be the domination number of $G$, and let $\rho_G$ denote its normalised domination density. **$k$-regular bipartite domination number bound.** For every such graph,

$$
\gamma(G)\leq 2\left\lceil \frac{n}{k}\right\rceil, \qquad \rho_G\leq\frac{1}{n}\left\lceil \frac{n}{k}\right\rceil.
$$

The bound is proposed as a route toward proving Vizing's conjecture for balanced $k$-regular bipartite graphs. It is not proved in full generality and is used in the paper to reduce the remaining verification to finitely many unresolved cases.

370352.title: The 1/3–2/3 conjecture for linear extensions of posets
370352.ordinary_result_or_gap: Literal all finite nonchain posets; large-width asymptotic balance theorem 2609.30895 does not imply the universal 1/3 bound for remaining finite bounded-width posets. Prior-family match is not a complete public-resolution bridge. No full proof claimed.
370352.literal_statement:
Let $P$ be a finite poset that is not a chain. For distinct $x,y\in P$, write $\delta_{xy}=\min\\{p(x\prec y),p(y\prec x)\\}$ and $\delta(P)=\max_{x\ne y}\delta_{xy}$. **The 1/3–2/3 conjecture.**

$$
\delta(P)\geq \frac13.
$$

This is a central balancing conjecture for uniformly random linear extensions. It was proposed by Kislitsyn and independently by Fredman and Linial; the conjecture remains open in general, although many special classes of posets are known and a positive universal constant is known.

370371.title: The associated-prime persistence conjecture for homological shift ideals
370371.ordinary_result_or_gap: All polymatroidal ideals and i>0, starting k=i. Homological shifts being polymatroidal alone does not imply cross-power associated-prime inclusions. Need a compatible localization/socle witness from k to k+1 uniformly in i. Known i=1 and special ideals are partial.
370371.literal_statement:
Let $S$ be the polynomial ring in the paper, let $I\subset S$ be a polymatroidal ideal, and let $\operatorname{HS}_i(I^k)$ denote the $i$th homological shift ideal of $I^k$. **Associated-prime persistence conjecture.** For every $i>0$, the associated-prime sequence is an increasing chain beginning at the $i$th power:

$$
\operatorname{Ass}\,\operatorname{HS}_i(I^{i})\subset\operatorname{Ass}\,\operatorname{HS}_i(I^{i+1})\subset\operatorname{Ass}\,\operatorname{HS}_i(I^{i+2})\subset\cdots.
$$

The assertion is proved in the paper for principal Borel ideals, polymatroidal ideals satisfying the strong exchange property, and matroidal edge ideals; it remains open for arbitrary polymatroidal ideals.

370678.title: The finite-orbit bound conjecture for the curve graph of spherical Artin–Tits groups
370678.ordinary_result_or_gap: All spherical Artin-Tits groups of rank n. Braid Proposition 33 has bound n+1, but per-element centralizer periodicity is not rank-uniform. Need uniform control of eigenvalue root-of-unity ratios and its orbit transfer; no full route.
370678.literal_statement: Let $G$ be an Artin-Tits group of spherical type with rank $n$, let $\mathcal C(G)$ be the curve graph, and let $\alpha\in G$. Consider a vertex of $\mathcal C(G)$ with a finite orbit under the action of $\alpha$. **Finite-orbit bound conjecture.** The size of every such finite orbit is bounded above by a number depending only on $n$. The conjecture is proved in the paper for braid groups, where every finite orbit has size at most $n+1$; its status for general spherical Artin–Tits groups is not resolved in the source.

370871.title: Refined $q,t$-symmetry conjecture for $\vec{k}$-Dyck paths with $a$- and $b$-tails
370871.ordinary_result_or_gap: Actual source Conjecture 1.4 is over the whole rearrangement family with fixed a and b tails; one ordered path polynomial can fail symmetry (Example 1.5). Nearby Theorem 1.2 for no tails cannot be substituted. Journal DOI 10.1016/j.aam.2026.103099 unread. No all-tail weight-switching map proved.
370871.literal_statement:
Let $\vec{k}$ be a vector of positive integers, let $\mathcal{K}$ denote the corresponding parameter indexing the relevant $\vec{k}$-Dyck paths, and let $\widetilde{C}_{\mathcal{K}^{a}\mathcal{K}^{b}}(q,t)$ be the refined polynomial graded by the statistics area and depth. A polynomial is $q,t$-symmetric when $F(q,t)=F(t,q)$. **The $(a,b)$-tail symmetry conjecture.** For every positive integer vector $\vec{k}$ and all positive integers $a$ and $b$,

$$
\widetilde{C}_{\mathcal{K}^{a}\mathcal{K}^{b}}(q,t)=\widetilde{C}_{\mathcal{K}^{a}\mathcal{K}^{b}}(t,q).
$$

The paper presents this as the second conjecture in its refined $q,t$-symmetry program. The nearby theorems prove symmetry for related refined polynomials, while the status of this stronger claim is left open in the supplied text.

371103.title: Desarguesian conjecture for cyclic projective planes
371103.ordinary_result_or_gap: Every finite cyclic projective plane must be Desarguesian. Source Hall/Singer construction and forbidden finite Sidon-set result are one direction/examples, not all cyclic-plane classification. No finite non-Desarguesian cyclic object or full proof route; recent source date does not make this new.
371103.literal_statement:
A **cyclic projective plane** is a projective plane admitting a regular action by a cyclic group. A projective plane is **Desarguesian** when it satisfies Desargues's theorem, and a perfect difference set gives rise to a cyclic projective plane. **Desargues's conjecture.** Every finite cyclic projective plane, and hence every corresponding perfect difference set, is Desarguesian.

This conjecture would provide an alternative route to the paper's main theorem because Desargues's theorem imposes strong geometric restrictions. The source explicitly says that the conjecture is open; Hall described the assertion as highly plausible.

371304.title: The population-preservation conjecture for consecutive pattern avoidance
371304.ordinary_result_or_gap: Source (1.1) is an asymptotic expected occurrence density. E[Xp]=o(n) does not control Pr(Xp=0), nor conditional q-density. Both finite-state and repair-injection routes lack the exact permutation measure bridge. Full attempts and missing estimates recorded.
371304.literal_statement:
For $m>0$, let $p_1,\ldots,p_k,p$ be consecutive patterns of length $m$. Define

$$
\mathcal{A}_n=\textsc{Av}_n(p_1,\ldots,p_k),\qquad \mathcal{B}_n=\textsc{Av}_n(p_1,\ldots,p_k,p).
$$

Suppose that $\textsc{pop}_{\mathcal{A}}(p)=0$. **Population-preservation conjecture.** For every consecutive pattern $q$ of length $m$, we have

$$
\textsc{pop}_{\mathcal{B}}(q)=\textsc{pop}_{\mathcal{A}}(q).
$$

The conjecture is true for the cases solved in the paper, while its validity in general remains an open question.
